canonical_definition:
What it is. Across papers, the prevailing usage is a human evaluation protocol run on the same benchmark tasks as a model, to provide a performance reference, baseline, or upper-bound. Most definitions describe people completing prompts, puzzles, questions, web or OS tasks, extraction tasks, or meal-estimation examples, with variants ranging from independent annotators and native speakers to domain experts, authors, volunteers, Prolific participants, and humans acting as LLM agents. A smaller line of work uses closely related procedures such as expert forecasts or an offline survey in which participants view clues, submit a guess after each clue, and indicate whether they would buzz. Some implementations cover the full task set, while others are restricted to subsets such as 100 randomly selected table-updating pairs, 75 abstracts, or 1000 questions.

What it is claimed to measure. Papers do not record this instrument as measuring any construct or behavioral indicator: it is linked to no constructs and no behavioral indicators. The only explicit relational claim is that one paper uses a human baseline to measure OSWorld, and reports that the human performance study shows OSWorld examples are more time-consuming and challenging than prior work.

Space of uses. Across papers, it is usually presented inside another benchmark or dataset as a comparison procedure for model results. Authors use it to contextualize model scores, provide a human-level reference, verify answerability or consistency, or compare time, efficiency, and accuracy, and the only explicit linked instrument is OSWorld. The reported forms range from small-scale studies with authors and naive volunteers, to expert and native-speaker evaluations, to larger user studies and human-acting-as-agent setups.

Concerns raised. One paper states that its human-baseline evaluation was restricted to 100 randomly selected table-updating pairs because of cost and time constraints. Another notes that expert forecasts were only available for some studies.

definitions.text: A human performance benchmark for information updating, derived from independent annotators manually synchronizing tables, used to compare model outputs on a subset of 100 examples.
definitions.paper: Leveraging LLM For Synchronizing Information Across Multilingual Tables

definitions.text: A protocol where human participants attempt tasks from the benchmark to establish a baseline for success rates and efficiency, with evaluation conducted by a third party.
definitions.paper: VideoWebArena:  Evaluating Long Context Multimodal Agents with Video Understanding Web Tasks

definitions.text: An evaluation protocol where human participants (computer science students) perform the benchmark tasks to establish a baseline for performance, time, and accuracy.
definitions.paper: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments

definitions.text: A study conducted with human participants to establish a baseline for Wisdom of Crowds effects in guesstimation tasks and to compare human performance with that of LLMs.
definitions.paper: Probing LLM World Models: Enhancing Guesstimation with Wisdom of Crowds Decoding

definitions.text: A human evaluation in which human participants acted as LLM agents to complete EnterpriseBench tasks, used to measure upper-bound performance and compare against model agents.
definitions.paper: Can LLMs Help You at Work? A Sandbox for Evaluating LLM Agents in Enterprise Environments

definitions.text: An evaluation protocol where human experts predict research outcomes, used as a performance baseline to compare against LLM simulation accuracy.
definitions.paper: Position: LLM Social Simulations Are a Promising Research Method

definitions.text: A human evaluation procedure where professional nutritionists provide carbohydrate estimates for a subset of meal descriptions to compare against LLM performance.
definitions.paper: NutriBench: A Dataset for Evaluating Large Language Models in Nutrition Estimation from Meal Descriptions

definitions.text: A human evaluation protocol where domain experts, such as computational biologists, perform a task like hypothesis validation, and their performance and process are compared against an automated system.
definitions.paper: Automated Hypothesis Validation with Agentic Sequential Falsifications

definitions.text: A user study with 204 participants recruited via Prolific, comparing human and agent engagement behaviors on curated social media snapshots containing factual and false news articles.
definitions.paper: MOSAIC: Modeling Social AI for Content Dissemination and Regulation in Multi-Agent Simulations

definitions.text: A data collection procedure where human participants view a sequence of clues for held-out questions and submit a guess after each clue, also indicating whether they would choose to 'buzz' at that point.
definitions.paper: GRACE: A Granular Benchmark for Evaluating Model Calibration against Human Calibration

definitions.text: An evaluation protocol where human experts (six Ph.D. candidates in chemistry) solve puzzles from the MolPuzzle benchmark to establish a performance baseline for comparison with LLMs.
definitions.paper: Can LLMs Solve Molecule Puzzles? A Multimodal Benchmark for Molecular Structure Elucidation

definitions.text: An evaluation protocol comparing LLM scores on CTF challenges against scores achieved by human participants in the same competitions.
definitions.paper: NYU CTF Bench: A Scalable Open-Source Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating LLMs in Offensive Security

definitions.text: An evaluation protocol where 10 human volunteers perform the benchmark tasks to establish a performance reference point.
definitions.paper: Optimus-1: Hybrid Multimodal Memory Empowered Agents Excel in Long-Horizon Tasks

definitions.text: An evaluation protocol to verify dataset answerability by measuring human accuracy on a randomly selected subset of questions and corresponding document images.
definitions.paper: WildDoc: How Far Are We from Achieving Comprehensive and Robust Document Understanding in the Wild?

definitions.text: A native-speaker human evaluation using five annotators per language to provide reference performance for the benchmark.
definitions.paper: TVQACML: Benchmarking Text-Centric Visual Question Answering in Multilingual Chinese Minority Languages

relationships.evidence: The human performance study indicates that task examples from OSWORLD are more time-consuming and challenging compared to those in prior work. (Section 3.2)
